clue.text: All but happy whipping free bits of tack

indicators.note: all but a word means every letter of it except the last one
whipping is binding cord tightly round something, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: blest is a poetic spelling of blessed, happy
to rid is to free, as in rid of a burden

explanation.surface: A cruel rider is whipping a horse free of its harness, which hardly makes anyone happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Blest is the poetic spelling of blessed. 'Whipping' in the surface suggests flogging; in the wordplay it is binding round, as cord is whipped round a rope's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridles are headgear with bit and reins, part of a horse's tack, the riding equipment.

clue.text: Bishop, one old senior servant, from the south to give approval

indicators.note: in a down entry, starting from the south means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
I is the Roman numeral one
a pug was once the name for an upper servant in a large household

explanation.surface: A bishop and a head butler come up to give their blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: Pug as a senior servant is an obsolete sense, also a pet name, not the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To big up is slang for praising or talking someone up, which is giving approval.

clue.text: I am about to fly, maybe

definitions.text: I am about to fly, maybe

blocks.note: the usual contraction
a is an old preposition meaning on or about, as in a-hunting
to fly is to go quickly

explanation.surface: An insect announces it is ready to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the adult insect speaks, having emerged ready to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final winged adult stage of an insect, the stage at which it can fly.

clue.text: Singer oppressed by underworld Mafiosi's at a leap (7, two words)

indicators.note: in a down entry, being pressed down by something means sitting underneath it

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the underworld itself
an alto is a singer with a low voice

explanation.surface: A singer is bullied by a gangland Mafia boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Mafiosi signals an Italian phrase, and the underworld here is classical, not criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Di salto is Italian for at a leap or at one bound, so it is the Mafiosi's way of saying it.

clue.text: The old curse for example ahead of active duty

indicators.note: ahead of fixes the order, putting the first piece above the second

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
AD is the abbreviation for active duty

explanation.surface: A veteran swearing before going back on active service.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old mild oath, a minced form of by God, so a curse no longer used.

clue.text: Irish toast is not commonly seen in odd spots in Selsey

indicators.note: the odd spots in a word are its first, third and fifth places
seen in places the first piece inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: letters one, three and five
ain't is the colloquial form of is not

explanation.surface: An Irish drinking toast is rarely heard here and there in Selsey, a Sussex seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Slainte, meaning health, is the Irish and Scottish Gaelic toast said when raising a glass.

clue.text: Weight trouble? Cereal's your answer

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for weight
heat is pressure or trouble, as in the police turning up the heat

explanation.surface: A diet advert: worried about your weight? Eat cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a cereal grass, the grain milled for flour.

clue.text: Form of charter, eg, we Latins developed

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new form, so the letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Romance-language speakers invented a way of hiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet-leasing is the hire of an aircraft along with its crew, a form of charter arrangement.

clue.text: End of the British Legion is a devil

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the final letter
the initials of British Legion
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares the demise of the British Legion, the veterans' charity, to be diabolical.
explanation.definitionFit: Eblis, or Iblis, is the chief devil in Islamic tradition.

clue.text: Craving forgotten purpose apparently for Provençal

indicators.note: X for Y means put the first piece where the second used to be

blocks.note: pretence once meant purpose or intention, a sense now forgotten
app. is the abbreviation for apparently
Pr. is the abbreviation for Provençal

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a lost purpose, which seems Provençal in style.
explanation.walkthrough: PR is removed from the front of PRETENCE and APP put in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetence is a desire or strong appetite for something, the same as a craving.

clue.text: Drink group filling up? Great

blocks.note: tea is a drink
a ring is a group of people, as in a spy ring
a hint at a second sense: eyes welling with moisture

explanation.surface: A drinks party fills up nicely; terrific.
explanation.walkthrough: The query on filling up points to a second sense, eyes welling with tears, alongside the main definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing is an old informal adjective meaning tremendous or splendid, as in a tearing success.

clue.text: Mixed in with m-merciless tyrant and called the shots

blocks.note: I is used as a short form of in
Ming the Merciless, the Flash Gordon villain, with the stammered initial doubled
whoever calls the shots is in charge, so led

explanation.surface: Someone joined a pitiless tyrant and gave orders alongside him.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in m-merciless is the setter's hint to double the M of Ming, the tyrant of the Flash Gordon comics.
explanation.definitionFit: To immingle is an old verb meaning to blend or mingle together, so immingled is mixed.

clue.text: See Government file that's coarse

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for government
a rasp is a coarse file with raised teeth

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a rough government dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: The file here is the tool for smoothing wood, not a folder of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to understand, and to grasp an idea is to understand it.

clue.text: Take in huntswoman, say, with a stint as flirt

indicators.note: take in means putting the first piece inside the next

blocks.note: a pink is a fox-hunter, from the pink coat worn in the hunting field
R, recipe, is the abbreviation for take on prescriptions
the a taken as written
a bout is a spell or stint of activity

explanation.surface: A woman out hunting is invited to spend a spell as a coquette.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunting pink is the scarlet coat of the hunt, so a pink is a rider wearing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prink about is to strut and show off one's finery, the behaviour of a flirt.

clue.text: Thanks surrounding tips from Alec Leamus, presumably unearthing a mole

indicators.note: the tips of words are their front ends, so take the opening letter of each
surrounding means one piece goes round the outside of the others

blocks.note: ta is informal British thanks
initials of the three words

explanation.surface: Gratitude to Alec Leamas, the Le Carré spy who came in from the cold, for exposing a double agent.
explanation.walkthrough: Alec Leamas is the hero of The Spy Who Came in from the Cold, so a mole seems to mean a double agent; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Talpa is Latin for mole and the scientific genus name of the European mole.

clue.text: What's in bottom drawer? Sort us out with Evian, say

indicators.note: out means disordered or not in the right state, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange
Evian is a brand of French mineral water, eau in French

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help clearing a drawer and is offered bottled water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort us out' reads as one phrase; Sort is part of the fodder and out is the signal. A bottom drawer is British for the store a bride-to-be keeps for married life.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects for her marriage, kept in the bottom drawer.

clue.text: Mick Dundee's comparatively daft restraint about recliner

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read from the other end

blocks.note: a lid keeps something in check, as in keeping a lid on it
one who lies down

explanation.surface: Crocodile Dundee is sillier than a man held back on a reclining chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick 'Crocodile' Dundee is the film Australian, which marks the definition as Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilly is Australian slang for foolish or crazy, and dillier is its comparative form.

clue.text: Macrology is feasible ringing 59 in journalism

indicators.note: ringing means forming a ring around the next piece
in places the whole built piece inside the following word

blocks.note: the press is journalism collectively
on means possible, as in that's not on
LIX is 59 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dry note that waffling is acceptable in newspaper writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest one inside the other, and 'on' meaning feasible is the sense in 'that's just not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macrology is a rare word for long-winded talk, which is exactly wordiness or verbosity.

clue.text: Scots trap blooming Nationalist in fit of sulks

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or peevishness
flowers that are blooming are out
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: A Scottish nationalist sulks over a trap set for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A pout-net is a Scottish name for a fishing net shaped like a funnel, a trap for fish.

clue.text: Place a university named for French approval

blocks.note: Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for Place
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
dit is French for said or named

explanation.surface: A college is named in French acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or applause, an act of approval.

clue.text: Isolate English with numerical control over Scottish remainder

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above the piece that follows

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
NC is the abbreviation for numerical control in machining
lave is Scots for the rest or remainder

explanation.surface: Cut off the English, with machines controlling the rest of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclave is to surround and so shut off a territory, isolating it inside another.

clue.text: One vociferous revolutionary holding nuke, say

indicators.note: say asks for words as spoken, with the spelling to be worked out afterwards

blocks.note: to own is to hold, and N is the abbreviation for nuclear

explanation.surface: A loudmouth rebel has his hands on a nuclear weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Owen Glendower led the Welsh revolt against Henry IV, and Shakespeare makes him a loud boaster who can call spirits from the vasty deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen Glendower was a Welsh rebel leader, a revolutionary given a boastful voice by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Fished and messed about without pressure

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: to potter is to mess about doing small jobs
P is the abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone spent a lazy day angling and pottering, free of stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To otter is to fish with an otter board, a float trailing many baited lines.

clue.text: Turn over mostly pedestrian game

mostly means most of a word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over
pedestrian means dull and uninspired

explanation.surface: A dreary board game is mostly about turning things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over' looks like one phrase, but over is a piece of the wordplay; DUL follows O, and then the lot is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Settling mostly new point in epigram

indicators.note: mostly means most of a word, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
the sting of an epigram is its sharp closing point

explanation.surface: A writer settles on a fresh point to round off a witty saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting is settling into a home, as birds do when they build and occupy a nest.

clue.text: Signs of change help returning reviewers

blocks.note: aid means help
critics review books, plays and films

explanation.surface: Reviewers coming back to help is a sign that things are changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Diacritics are marks such as accents and cedillas that show a letter's sound is altered.

clue.text: Flipping smashed exam entering college — it'll help travel

blocks.note: a student who smashed an exam aced it

the front half

clue.text: Working girls from around the Seine plying River Ouse
